quests.instruction: A hungry bird hops along a green leaf and doesn't notice the animal lying on it. Which animal is hardest to spot?
quests.hint: Its body colour matches the leaf it's sitting on.
quests.explanation: Colours and patterns that match the background are called camouflage. A green caterpillar on a green leaf is very hard for a bird to see.
quests.funFact: Some caterpillars look so much like bird droppings that birds leave them alone.
quests.question: Caterpillar

quests.instruction: Find the hunter that hides in dry leaves, its patterned scales matching the ground, until food comes close.
quests.hint: Its pattern looks like the ground it lies on.
quests.explanation: Camouflage helps hunters as well as hiders. A snake whose pattern matches leaves or sand can lie hidden until prey gets close.
quests.funFact: A patterned snake lying still can look just like a twig.
quests.question: Snake

quests.instruction: Which animal's skin can change colour and bumpiness in a flash to match rocks or seaweed?
quests.hint: Special cells in its skin act like tiny colour pixels.
quests.explanation: An octopus has colour cells in its skin and can change how bumpy it looks, so it blends into the seabed.
quests.funFact: An octopus can change colour in less than a second.
quests.question: Octopus

quests.instruction: Which insect's yellow-and-black stripes warn other animals that it can sting?
quests.hint: Its bold colours mean "keep away".
quests.explanation: Bright, bold patterns often warn enemies that an animal is dangerous or tastes bad.
quests.funFact: A honey bee that stings a mammal usually loses its stinger and can't sting again.
quests.question: Bee

quests.instruction: Name the hopper that can lean back on its strong tail and kick an attacker with both back feet.
quests.hint: Its tail acts as a third leg when it balances.
quests.explanation: A kangaroo can balance on its tail and kick with powerful hind legs, which is a strong defence.
quests.funFact: A kangaroo's tail is so strong that it works like a fifth leg when it walks slowly.
quests.question: Kangaroo

quests.instruction: Which animal's thick, tough skin is folded into plates like armour?
quests.hint: Thorns and bites hardly bother it.
quests.explanation: A rhino's skin is thick and tough. It protects the rhino from thorns and bites.
quests.funFact: Even with such thick skin, rhinos can get sunburnt, so they roll in mud.
quests.question: Rhino

quests.instruction: Which swimmer's very thick, oily fur traps air against its skin and keeps it warm in cold water?
quests.hint: It has no blubber, so its fur has to do all the work.
quests.explanation: Otters have dense fur that traps a layer of air next to their skin. That keeps heat in and cold water out.
quests.funFact: Sea otters spend a lot of time grooming to keep their fur clean and fluffy.
quests.question: Otter

quests.instruction: Which desert hare's very long ears help it lose extra body heat?
quests.hint: Its big ears work a bit like radiators.
quests.explanation: A jackrabbit's long ears are full of blood vessels. Heat can escape from them into the air to cool the animal.
quests.funFact: Jackrabbits can run in zigzags to escape a hunter.
quests.question: Jackrabbit

quests.instruction: Which pet cools itself by panting, because it can't sweat much through its skin?
quests.hint: Moving air over its wet tongue carries heat away.
quests.explanation: Dogs have few sweat glands, so they cool off by panting. Air passing over the wet tongue takes heat away.
quests.funFact: Dogs do sweat a little, through their paw pads.
quests.question: Dog

quests.instruction: Which animal's smooth, tapered body slices through water, though it's clumsy on land?
quests.hint: Its shape is a bit like a torpedo.
quests.explanation: A smooth, pointed body shape slips through water with little drag. On land the seal's flippers make it flop along.
quests.funFact: A diving seal can slow its heartbeat to save oxygen.
quests.question: Seal

quests.instruction: Which animal's heavy, barrel-shaped body lets it walk along a riverbed?
quests.hint: It's so heavy that it sinks, instead of swimming.
quests.explanation: Hippos can't really swim. Their heavy bodies sink, so they walk or push off along the bottom of rivers.
quests.funFact: A hippo can close its nostrils and hold its breath for several minutes.
quests.question: Hippo

quests.instruction: Which tall animal's long legs and neck give it a lookout view over the plains?
quests.hint: Standing tall means it can see danger a long way off.
quests.explanation: A giraffe can spot trouble from far away. Its long legs also let it gallop off quickly.
quests.funFact: A giraffe can run about 55 kilometres an hour for short distances.
quests.question: Giraffe

quests.instruction: Which sleepy tree-dweller gets most of its water from the leaves it eats, so it hardly ever drinks?
quests.hint: Its leafy meals contain a lot of moisture.
quests.explanation: Koalas get most of the water they need from eucalyptus leaves, so they rarely need to drink.
quests.funFact: Koalas have rough pads on their paws that grip smooth tree trunks.
quests.question: Koala

quests.instruction: Which tiny desert animal digs a burrow to escape the midday heat and can live on the moisture in seeds?
quests.hint: It stays underground when the sun is high.
quests.explanation: Some desert rodents sleep in cool burrows by day and get water from the seeds they eat.
quests.funFact: Many desert mice are active only at night, when the air is cooler.
quests.question: Mouse

quests.instruction: In a desert morning fog, which little insect tilts its bumpy back so drops of water roll into its mouth?
quests.hint: It stands head-down in the mist.
quests.explanation: In the Namib Desert, certain beetles collect fog on their bumpy backs. The drops roll down toward their mouths.
quests.funFact: Scientists have copied this beetle's back to design nets that collect water from fog.
quests.question: Beetle

quests.instruction: Which sea animal sends out clicks and listens to the echoes to find fish in murky water?
quests.hint: Its ears hear sounds that bounce back.
quests.explanation: Dolphins make clicks and listen to the echoes. The echoes tell them the size, shape and distance of what's ahead.
quests.funFact: A dolphin can use clicks to find prey hidden in sand.
quests.question: Dolphin

quests.instruction: Name the animal that can pick up the faint smell of blood from far across the water.
quests.hint: Its sense of smell is one of its strongest tools.
quests.explanation: Sharks can detect tiny traces of scent in the water. They can also sense faint electric signals from other animals.
quests.funFact: Sharks have tiny pores on their snouts that sense electric signals from other animals.
quests.question: Shark

quests.instruction: Spot the animal that rests a leg on a silk thread and feels a tiny tug when an insect gets stuck.
quests.hint: It can feel shaking that you can't even see.
quests.explanation: Spiders feel vibrations through the silk and through sensors on their legs, so they know when something lands in the web.
quests.funFact: A spider's legs are covered in fine hairs that are sensitive to touch and air movement.
quests.question: Spider

quests.instruction: A very long, showy tail makes flying and running harder. Which bird has one anyway, to impress a mate?
quests.hint: The feature isn't for hiding. It's for being noticed.
quests.explanation: A peacock's tail isn't for survival. It's a display to impress peahens, even though it makes escaping harder.
quests.funFact: A peacock's train of feathers can be more than a metre and a half long.
quests.question: Peacock

quests.instruction: Pick the small rainforest animal that has bright skin as a warning that it's poisonous.
quests.hint: The brighter its skin, the more dangerous it is to eat.
quests.explanation: Some rainforest frogs have vivid colours and poison. Predators learn to avoid them.
quests.funFact: Poison dart frogs get their poison from the insects they eat in the wild.
quests.question: Poison Dart Frog

quests.instruction: Large eye-like spots on its wings startle a bird that was about to peck. Which insect?
quests.hint: The spots look like the eyes of a bigger animal.
quests.explanation: Eyespots can startle predators, who may mistake them for the eyes of a bigger animal. That gives the insect time to escape.
quests.funFact: Some butterflies have a plain top side and show their eyespots only when they open their wings.
quests.question: Butterfly

quests.instruction: Thin mountain air has little oxygen. Which woolly animal has blood that carries oxygen well and a thick coat for the cold?
quests.hint: It lives high in the Andes.
quests.explanation: Llamas live high in the Andes. Their blood carries oxygen very well, which helps them in the thin air, and their wool keeps them warm.
quests.funFact: A llama can carry about a quarter of its own body weight.
quests.question: Llama

quests.instruction: Name the shaggy animal that swings its heavy head from side to side like a snowplough to uncover grass in winter.
quests.hint: It uses its head as a shovel.
quests.explanation: Bison sweep snow aside with their big heads to reach the grass beneath. Their thick coat keeps them warm.
quests.funFact: A bison's winter coat is so thick that snow can sit on its back without melting.
quests.question: Bison

quests.instruction: Which swimming bird has tightly overlapping feathers, a layer of fat, and oil to keep icy water out?
quests.hint: Its feathers work like tiles on a roof.
quests.explanation: Penguin feathers overlap like roof tiles and trap air, and a layer of fat adds more warmth.
quests.funFact: Penguins spread oil from a gland near the tail over their feathers to keep them waterproof.
quests.question: Penguin

quests.instruction: Spring comes early and the snow melts. Which white-coated animal is now easy to spot against bare brown ground?
quests.hint: Its winter fur was a perfect match for snow, but not for mud.
quests.explanation: An Arctic fox's white winter coat hides it in snow. When the snow melts early, the white fur stands out on the ground.
quests.funFact: An Arctic fox's thick fur keeps it warm even in extreme cold.
quests.question: Arctic Fox

quests.instruction: A pond dries up in summer. Which animal can most easily travel to a new one?
quests.hint: Think about which one can cross land or air quickly.
quests.explanation: A duck can fly to another pond. Fish can't leave the water, and snails move very slowly.
quests.funFact: Ducks can carry seeds and tiny animals' eggs on their feet and feathers to new ponds.
quests.question: Duck

quests.instruction: Food is hard to find in winter. Which spiky animal fattens up in autumn, then sleeps through the cold months?
quests.hint: It tucks itself into a nest of leaves.
quests.explanation: Hedgehogs build fat in autumn, then hibernate. Their bodies slow right down to save energy.
quests.funFact: A hibernating hedgehog's heart beats very slowly.
quests.question: Hedgehog

quests.instruction: Forward-facing eyes, sharp talons and wings that make no noise: which night hunter?
quests.hint: Its wings are built to be quiet.
quests.explanation: Forward-facing eyes judge distance, talons grab, and soft-edged feathers keep the wings quiet. Together they make a great night hunter.
quests.funFact: Owls have three eyelids: one for blinking, one for sleeping and one for cleaning.
quests.question: Owl

quests.instruction: Find the great ape that walks on its knuckles because its arms are so long and strong.
quests.hint: Look at what its hands are doing when it walks on all fours.
quests.explanation: Gorillas walk on their knuckles. Their long arms hold up the front of their bodies.
quests.funFact: A gorilla's arm span can be wider than the animal is tall.
quests.question: Gorilla

quests.instruction: Which animal's dry, scaly skin keeps water in, so it can live in hot, dry places?
quests.hint: The others have damp skin that dries out fast.
quests.explanation: Reptile scales make a waterproof layer, so lizards lose little water. Frogs and worms have damp skin that dries out quickly.
quests.funFact: Lizards shed their old skin as they grow.
quests.question: Lizard
